walkthrough: Goal: after practising stage 1, see my copy's errors down to a pen's width when I compare, have Aligned show at once rather than make me wait, and see a box's extensions without them covering the original I copy from.
A line: Today, Start practice, Got it. I copy the first line with Draw, its upper half close and its lower half drifting a pen's width or two to the right, as a hand does.

Compare, In place: the original lies over my line in red as thick as my pen and see-through. Where my line follows it, my ink shows through the red as a darker red; where I strayed, the light red and my black ink lie side by side, a pen's width apart. Aligned: the original moves and sizes onto my line at once (the card's 'Aligning…' no longer stays), so only the shape's error shows, here the lower end leaning. Two fingers spread over my copy to 400 %: the red stays as thick as my pen there too, so the gap between them is wide on the screen; In place there, the drift at the lower end is plain. Pinched to the whole sheet, the red thins with the view but never below a hairline.

A group: back in the gallery and Continue practice, the sheet opens where I was; Next on to the first combined lines (their instructions, Got it). I draw both lines, the first a pen's width left of its original in its middle, the second ending a little high. Compare: the whole group in the thin see-through red in place, then Aligned as one shape; at 400 % each line's error shows beside its original.

A shape: the gallery's practice options import a pack, and Stage 2 starts at once: a warm-up of three, then the first single shape (its instructions, Got it). I draw its outline a little off and a line inside. Compare: the picture faint over my copy with its outline in the same thin see-through red, in place, then Aligned (the line inside never pulls it); at 400 % the outline lies on my ink, darker where they agree.

A box: Continue practice, Next past the other shapes and the colour work to the box (its instructions, Got it). I draw its nine edges, one top edge turned off. Compare: the exact box red over mine, as thick as my pen; each of my edges drawn on dashed towards its vanishing point. The left point lies inside the original's frame: the dashes stop at that frame's side and no ring is drawn there, so the original's own box and lines stay clear; past my frame on the right the dashes run on to the right point, ringed. The card: 8 of 9 edges head for their vanishing point.
Nothing to undo or keep: the overlay is the screen's, never the artwork's; the strokes are as they were drawn.

Not here: free boxes, which s84-perspective walks (their extensions alike) and the tablet reaches with practice-test start 2 2; the 2° a free box's edge may miss by (the author's, after practising free boxes).
